newsitem.title: HONG KONG: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sept 26.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - HK newspaper headlines - Sept 26.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Hong Kong press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- ORIENTAL DAILY NEWS -- Protesters on the Diaoyu Islands protest ship had started arguing with each other and refused to cook food for the journalists on board.

-- MING PAO DAILY NEWS -- China published the full list of some 5,700 nominees for the 400-strong Selection Committee which would appoint Hong Kong's first chief executive and legislature after the handover.

-- Chief Justice Sir T.L. Yang said that Beijing did not know how to package its image and that Hong Kong people paid too much attention to appearance. He said that the difference led to many misunderstandings.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC TIMES -- Lawyers in China were getting rich quickly by setting up their own law practices. A Beijing lawyer made over three million yuan last year. Some practices even bribed the leaders of state enterprises to get big cases.
-- The Mass Transit Railway Corp has invited developers to express their interest in deveoping the HK$3 billion hotel development at the Tai Kok Tsui station on the airport railway.

-- TA KUNG PAO -- Chinese foreign minister Qian Qichen made a speech at the United Nations general conference, stressing that a smooth Hong Kong handover should be ensured and that foreign interests in Hong Kong would be protected.

-- Qian Qichen reiterated China's sovereignty over the disputed Diaoyu Islands when meeting his Japanese counterpart in New York. He also stressed that the basic principle of developing a friendly relationship with Japan had not changed.

-- HONG KONG ECONOMIC JOURNAL -- Because Citic Pacific Ltd, the second biggest holder of Dragonair, was unwilling to have its stake decreased, Dragonair's plan to seek public listing had to be postponed to the end of next year.

-- SOUTH CHINA MORNING POST -- There were growing fears that an imminent report by United States Customs into alleged illegal textile transhipment would unveil wide-spread malpractice by Hong Kong's clothing manufacturers.

-- HONGKONG STANDARD -- According to figures released by the Hong Kong Monetary Authority, growth in the total value of mortgages outstanding took a larger than expected dip in August, which reflected a cooling in the property market.
